cases.name: #N: separated by spaces, or preceded or followed by punctuation
#N: not glued to a word, another reference or an entity
#N: glued to a letter other than an ascii one is a reference
leading zeros: in references and urls
GH-N: in any case, not glued to a word or a reference
owner/repo#N: not glued to a word or a dot, and the repository needs an owner
cases.markdown: actions/checkout#1. x.camunda/camunda#1 v4.2/foo#3 a.b/c#2 backport-action#706 korthout/backport-action#752abc

cases.name: owner/repo#N: not preceded by a slash
owner/repo#N: not at the end of a path, also one with a dot
owner/repo#N: not at the end of an absolute path
owner/repo#N: after punctuation other than a dot or a slash
owner/repo#N: not after a dot, like after a host such as gitlab.com
url: to an issue or pull request, with or without scheme
url: also with www.
same issue: listed once, as first written
same issue: written in full replaces a bare reference to the repository, in place
existence: issues and repositories aren't checked
url: other urls are plain links
paragraph text: headings, emphasis and tables don't hide references
setext heading: its text is linked
setext heading: its underline can end with spaces or tabs
thematic break: isn't a list item
thematic break: spaces or tabs between and after its markers
fenced code block: backticks or tildes, with an info string
fenced code block: interrupts a paragraph
fenced code block: closes with a fence of the same character, at least as long, without text
fenced code block: its closing fence can end with spaces or tabs
fenced code block: unclosed, hides the rest
fenced code block: only a tilde fence can have a backtick in its info string
indented code block: a tab after spaces advances to the next tab stop
indented code block: four spaces or a tab
indented code block: can't interrupt a paragraph
html block: a comment hides up to the line of its end, the rest of that line is visible
html block: an unclosed comment hides the rest
html block: pre hides its lines, also when unclosed
html block: other blocks like div and script don't hide
list item: its content column decides what is indented code
list item: one that starts with a blank line has its content 1 column after the marker
list item: a fenced code block ends with the item
list item: nested
list item: interrupts a paragraph
list item: one numbered other than 1 can't interrupt a paragraph
block quote: a fenced code block ends with the quote
block quote: indented code
block quote: lazy continuation
block quote: in a list item
code span: ends at a run of as many backticks
code span: across lines, but not across paragraphs
code span: unmatched backticks are literal
escape: a backslash makes the next character literal
comment: inline, also the short forms, hidden as a space
comment: unclosed in a paragraph is literal
comment: whichever opens first wins over a code span
html tag: hidden as a space with its attributes, and code, pre and a hide their content
html tag: text in angle brackets that isn't a tag is visible
autolink: its url is visible
link: text and title are hidden, also of an image
link: a destination that starts with a quote isn't a title, so a space inside it means it's no link
link: its destination counts when it's a url to an issue or pull request, not its text
link: its destination counts in order of occurrence
link: a destination that isn't a full url to an issue or pull request doesn't count
link: a destination with a trailing slash, query or fragment counts
link: hidden in code and comments, with its destination
reference link: the destination of its definition counts, the first definition of a label wins
html a element: its href counts when it's a url to an issue or pull request, not its content
html a element: without an href, like an anchor, it's no link and its content is visible
reference link: hidden only when its label is defined
reference link: a shortcut reference link can't be followed by a link label, which needs more than whitespace
reference link: only spaces, tabs and line endings are whitespace in a link label
link reference definition: its link label needs more than spaces, tabs and line endings, which are also all that's collapsed
reference link: in [a][b][c] with only c defined, [b][c] is the link
link reference definition: hidden, also in a container
link reference definition: not after a paragraph, in code, when invalid, or for a footnote
html entity: isn't a reference as written
html tag: an unclosed code element only hides the tag
blank line: only spaces and tabs, not other whitespace like a non-breaking space
line ending: a carriage return on its own also ends a line
gap: emphasis with underscores
cases.gap: Markdown reads `_` as emphasis here, the scanner reads it as part of a word

cases.name: gap: non-breaking space in a link destination or before a link title
cases.gap: Markdown only reads spaces, tabs and line endings as whitespace in a link, the scanner also other whitespace like a non-breaking space

cases.name: gap: link syntax like nested brackets
cases.gap: Markdown allows balanced brackets in link text, the scanner doesn't

cases.name: gap: link reference definition across lines
cases.gap: Markdown allows a link reference definition's title on the next line, the scanner doesn't

cases.name: gap: reference in the query or fragment of a url to an issue
cases.gap: Markdown links a url with its query and fragment, the scanner ends a url to an issue at its number and reads what follows as text

cases.name: gap: url right before a table cell
cases.gap: Markdown splits a table row into cells before it reads a url, the scanner reads a url up to the next whitespace, across a `|`

cases.name: gap: code span or html tag that starts in a link's text and ends after it
cases.gap: Markdown reads a code span, an autolink or an html tag before a link, the scanner reads the link first

cases.name: gap: github.com in capitals
cases.gap: A host name is the same in any case, the scanner only recognizes github.com in lowercase

cases.name: gap: code span in an html block
cases.gap: Markdown keeps the content of an html block as is, the scanner still reads code spans in it

cases.name: gap: fence in an html block
cases.gap: Markdown keeps the content of an html block as is up to a blank line, the scanner still opens a fenced code block in it

cases.name: gap: tab after a list item marker
cases.gap: Markdown expands a tab after a container marker to the next tab stop, the scanner only expands tabs at the start of a line

cases.name: gap: tab after a block quote marker
cases.gap: Markdown expands a tab after a container marker to the next tab stop, the scanner only expands tabs at the start of a line
